text.p: United Parcel Service and the Teamsters are "redoubling" their efforts to reach an agreement, officials from the Labor Department and federal mediation service said Friday.

"We think they are redoubling their efforts to reach an agreement," Susan King, spokeswoman for Labor Secretary Alexis Herman, said at a briefing in the Capitol Hill hotel where negotiations are underway.
Moments later her words were echoed by Dave Helfert, spokesman for the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service.
Without offering any specifics, King put the most optimistic face she could on the negotiations.

"We think the fact that they've been sitting for 20 1/2 hours talking, crunching numbers, moving back and forth between the caucus rooms and the together rooms, (means it) is clear that they are redoubling their efforts," she said.

The 12-day-old strike, which by company estimates has cost upwards of a half-billion dollars, has idled 185,000 Teamsters and shut down delivery of 90 percent of the 12 million packages daily usually sent by UPS.
